#!/usr/bin/env python3
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# COMPONENT: FIGJAM BOARD COMPOSITION
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

"""Turn a checked diagram model into the use_figma code that composes its board.

The board is drawn by `assets/compose-board.js`, which lays out and styles the
diagram itself: a framed board with a title block, tinted zones, shapes sized to
their text, routed connectors and a key. This script fills that file's MODEL from
the same parse `flow_check.py` checks, so the board holds exactly what passed the
check and the read-back counts it against the same numbers. A model that fails
the check is refused, because a composed board is as wrong as the model it drew.

Board text comes from comment lines the generator never needed, so the model
stays plain Mermaid:

- `%% title: Start a return` names the board, and falls back to a Mermaid
  frontmatter title, a sequence or gantt `title` line, then the diagram's place
- `%% subtitle: ...` is one sentence under the title on who reads it and why
- `%% source: ...` is the line under the key naming the sources and what was
  left out
- `%% zone: Find the order: orders, detail` groups nodes into a tinted zone. A
  user flow or a process without lanes reads its zones in flow order, an ER
  diagram draws each one around its entities, and lanes and composite states
  are zones already
- `%% focus: id` names the one thing the first glance lands on in a diagram
  that takes no `style` line: a node of an architecture, a state or an ER
  diagram, a message's number in a sequence, a task's id or name in a gantt.
  It is optional, and a user flow or a process marks its first glance with a
  `style` line instead

The board's style comes from `assets/figjam-design.md`, read over the composer's
built-in design by `figjam_checks/design.py`. Only the tokens it changes are
sent, in the code's THEME. A token that cannot stand falls back to its built-in
value and a design file that cannot be read falls back whole, each named on a
`DESIGN` line on stderr, so a bad edit never stops a board.

Usage:
  compose_board.py <model.md> [--diagram N] [--out path]  -> 0 the filled code is written, 1 the model fails
                                                             the check, 2 unreadable or no such diagram
  compose_board.py <model.md> --model                      -> print the MODEL as JSON instead of the code
  compose_board.py --template                              -> print the compact code with its MODEL and THEME
                                                             placeholders, the text the Project's composer
                                                             Knowledge file carries
  compose_board.py --design-check                          -> print the design a board is drawn in, what it
                                                             changes, its measures and the THEME it sends: 0 the
                                                             design reads with no warning, 1 one or more warnings
  compose_board.py --self-test                             -> prove every shipped model composes, its counts
                                                             match the check, the code fits one use_figma call and
                                                             the board it draws keeps its geometry and its design
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import copy
import io
import itertools
import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

import flow_check  # noqa: E402
import mermaid_extract  # noqa: E402
from figjam_checks import board_geometry as geometry  # noqa: E402
from figjam_checks import design as board_design  # noqa: E402
from figjam_checks import er, flowchart, gantt, sequence, state  # noqa: E402
from figjam_checks.board_fixtures import MODELS as DEFECT_MODELS, NEEDS_STACKING  # noqa: E402
from figjam_checks.common import ACCENT_PAIRS, CANVAS, content_lines, contrast, statements  # noqa: E402
from figjam_checks.layout import closing_edges  # noqa: E402

PROJECT_FENCE = re.compile(r"```javascript\n(.*?)\n```", re.S)

THEME_PLACEHOLDER = "__THEME__"

# use_figma takes at most 50,000 characters of code, and the model rides inside it.
MAX_CODE_CHARS = 50_000
# The composer's gap between two zones. A zone within two of them on any side sits beside it and takes another tint.
ZONE_GAP = 48
DIRECTIVE = re.compile(r"^\s*%%\s*(title|subtitle|source|zone|focus)\s*:\s*(.+?)\s*$", re.I)
ARCHITECTURE_KINDS = {"client": "client", "gateway": "gateway", "service": "service", "datastore": "datastore",
                      "external": "external", "async": "queue"}
FLOW_SHAPES = {"rhombus": "decision", "circle": "merge", "cylinder": "datastore", "subroutine": "subprocess",
               "parallelogram": "io"}
# A styled end names its own outcome: red marks a failure, any other accent the goal.
ERROR_FILLS = {"#ffcdc2"}
ARROWS = {"->>": "request", "-->>": "reply", "-)": "async", "--)": "asyncReply"}
# A gantt bar is placed in whole days on a date chart and in minutes on a one-day chart.
SECONDS_PER_DAY, SECONDS_PER_MINUTE = 86400, 60

# The code the composer reads for each end's mark: exactly one, zero or one, zero or more and one or more.
CARDINALITY_ENDS = {"||": "1", "|o": "?", "o|": "?", "}o": "*", "o{": "*", "}|": "+", "|{": "+"}


# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 1. BOARD TEXT AND ZONES
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def directives(block_text: str) -> tuple[dict[str, str], list[dict]]:
    """The title, subtitle and source comments, and the zones in the order they were written."""
    text, zones = {}, []
    for line in block_text.splitlines():
        match = DIRECTIVE.match(line)
        if not match:
            continue
        key, value = match.group(1).lower(), match.group(2)
        if key != "zone":
            text[key] = value
            continue
        label, _, members = value.rpartition(":")
        zone_id = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", label.strip().lower()).strip("-") or f"zone{len(zones) + 1}"
        zones.append({"id": zone_id, "label": label.strip(),
                      "members": [m.strip() for m in members.split(",") if m.strip()]})
    return text, zones


def zone_problems(zones: list[dict], node_ids: list[str], every_node: bool) -> list[str]:
    """A zone names nodes that exist, a node sits in one zone at most, and in flow order every node sits in one."""
    problems, owner = [], {}
    for zone in zones:
        if not zone["label"]:
            problems.append("a %% zone line has no label: write %% zone: Label: id, id")
        if not zone["members"]:
            problems.append(f"zone {zone['label']} names no node")
        for member in zone["members"]:
            if member not in node_ids:
                problems.append(f"zone {zone['label']} names {member}, which is no node in the diagram")
            elif member in owner:
                problems.append(f"node {member} sits in zones {owner[member]} and {zone['label']}: one zone each")
            else:
                owner[member] = zone["label"]
    if zones and every_node:
        loose = [node for node in node_ids if node not in owner]
        if loose:
            problems.append(f"{', '.join(loose)} sit in no zone: once a flow has zones, every node sits in one")
    return problems


FOCUS_LINE = re.compile(r"^\s*%%\s*focus\s*:", re.I | re.M)


def focus_problems(model: dict, profile: str, target: str, lines: int) -> list[str]:
    """Mark the one thing a `%% focus:` line names, or say why it names nothing."""
    if profile in (flowchart.USER_FLOW, flowchart.PROCESS):
        return ["%% focus on a user flow or a process: mark the first glance with a style line"]
    if lines > 1:
        return [f"{lines} %% focus lines, at most 1: the first glance is one thing"]
    if profile == "sequence":
        marked = model["messages"][int(target) - 1: int(target)] if target.isdigit() else []
        what = "a message number that exists"
    elif profile == "gantt":
        tasks = [task for section in model["sections"] for task in section["tasks"]]
        marked = [task for task in tasks if target in (task["id"], task["name"])][:1]
        what = "a task id or name"
    else:
        marked = [node for node in model["nodes"] if node["id"] == target][:1]
        what = "a node id"
    if not marked:
        return [f"%% focus: {target or '(empty)'} names nothing: write {what}"]
    marked[0]["accent"] = True
    return []


def board_title(block_text: str, text: dict[str, str], number: int) -> str:
    """The board's title: a `%% title:` line, a frontmatter title, a `title` line, then the diagram's place."""
    if text.get("title"):
        return text["title"]
    lines = content_lines(block_text)
    if lines and lines[0][1] == "---":
        for _, line in lines[1:]:
            if line == "---":
                break
            if line.lower().startswith("title:"):
                return line.split(":", 1)[1].strip().strip('"')
    for _, line in lines:
        if line.split()[0] == "title":
            return line[len("title"):].strip()
    return f"Diagram {number}"


# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 2. ONE MODEL PER KIND
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def accent_fills(block_text: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """The fill a `style` line gives each node, read the way the check reads it."""
    found = {}
    for statement in statements(block_text):
        words = statement.split()

            fill = flowchart.colour(statement, "fill")
            stroke = flowchart.colour(statement, "stroke")
            found[words[1]] = fill or flowchart.PAIRED_FILL.get(stroke, "")
    return found

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# COMPONENT: FIGJAM MODEL PRE-WRITE CHECK
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

"""Check a FigJam diagram model before it is written to a board.

A board is slow to fix once it exists: the composer owns its layout, so every
fix is a new write. Worse, neither the composer nor the generated fallback
draws all that Mermaid can say, so a model can promise a reader something the
board never shows. The rules each diagram kind carries are checked on the
Mermaid model first, and a model that breaks one is never written. The same
parse is measured, so a shape that is legal and still hard to read, such as a
rank of six steps or a connector that doubles back, is caught here rather than
on the board.

Each Mermaid block in the file is one diagram, read by its header:

- `flowchart` is a user flow unless a `%% type: process` or
  `%% type: architecture` comment line says otherwise
- `sequenceDiagram`, `stateDiagram-v2`, `erDiagram` and `gantt` are the other
  four kinds Flow Mode draws
- any other header, such as `pie`, `mindmap` or `journey`, is a kind Flow
  Mode does not draw and fails

The rules for each kind live in `figjam_checks/`, and `references/types/`
explains each one. Flowcharts and state diagrams are parsed by
`vendored/mermaid_extract.py`, a byte copy of the shared diagram skill's
extractor kept in step through `vendor.json`. It parses text only and never
renders or runs anything in a label. Sequence, ER and gantt blocks are parsed
by their own modules, because the extractor drops a sequence's dropped
features, the fields of an aliased entity and every gantt chart. Every
diagram of one flow runs the same direction, so two user flows or two
processes in one file must agree on it. A user flow and a process must also
carry one `style` line, because the board marks the first glance with its one
accent and has no other way to know where it falls.
A model that passes is composed into a board by `compose_board.py`, which keeps
its own self-test.

Usage:
  flow_check.py <model.md|model.mmd>  -> 0 every diagram passes, 1 a rule fails, 2 unreadable
  flow_check.py --self-test           -> prove each rule fails on a planted model with its own message,
                                         that the good models, the templates and the examples pass,
                                         and that the style guide's palette record still measures true
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import io
import re
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE / "vendored"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
import mermaid_extract  # noqa: E402
from figjam_checks import flowchart, layout  # noqa: E402
from figjam_checks.common import (
    ACCENT_PAIRS,
    CANVAS,
    CHARCOAL,
    LANE_PAIR,
    content_lines,
    contrast,
    type_directive,
)  # noqa: E402
from figjam_checks.er import check_er  # noqa: E402
from figjam_checks.gantt import check_gantt  # noqa: E402
from figjam_checks.sequence import check_sequence  # noqa: E402
from figjam_checks.state import check_state, check_state_header  # noqa: E402

PACKET = HERE.parent
FLOWCHART_TYPES = (flowchart.USER_FLOW, flowchart.PROCESS, flowchart.ARCHITECTURE)
HEADER_KINDS = {"flowchart": "flowchart", "graph": "flowchart", "sequencediagram": "sequence",
                "statediagram-v2": "state", "statediagram": "state", "erdiagram": "er", "gantt": "gantt"}
# Figma's list of kinds the board generator does not draw.
UNSUPPORTED = {"pie", "mindmap", "venn", "classdiagram", "journey", "timeline", "quadrantchart", "c4context",
               "c4container", "c4component", "c4dynamic", "c4deployment", "gitgraph", "requirementdiagram",
               "sankey-beta", "xychart-beta", "block-beta", "packet-beta", "architecture-beta", "kanban"}
NAMES = {"user-flow": "user flow", "process": "process", "architecture": "architecture", "sequence": "sequence",
         "state": "state", "er": "ER", "gantt": "gantt"}


# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 1. PROFILES AND CHECKS
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def header_word(block_text: str) -> str:
    """The first word of a block after any frontmatter, lowercased, which names its kind."""
    lines = content_lines(block_text)
    in_frontmatter = bool(lines) and lines[0][1] == "---"
    for _, text in lines[1:] if in_frontmatter else lines:
        if in_frontmatter:
            in_frontmatter = text != "---"
            continue
        return text.split()[0].lower()
    return ""


def profile_of(block_text: str) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
    """The profile a block is checked as, or an empty profile with the reason it has none."""
    word = header_word(block_text)
    directive = type_directive(block_text)
    if word in UNSUPPORTED:
        return "", [f"a {word} block: Flow Mode does not draw it, see references/flow-mode.md Section 3"]
    kind = HEADER_KINDS.get(word)
    if not kind:
        return "", [f"the block header {word or '(none)'} is no diagram kind Flow Mode draws"]
    if kind == "flowchart":
        directive = directive or flowchart.USER_FLOW
        if directive not in FLOWCHART_TYPES:
            return "", [f"%% type: {directive} is no flowchart type: write user-flow, process or architecture"]
        return directive, []
    if directive and directive != kind:
        return "", [f"%% type: {directive} on a {word} block: the header already names the kind"]
    return kind, []


def check_block(block: mermaid_extract.SourceBlock, block_text: str) -> tuple[str, list[str], str, str]:
    """Return the profile, its problems, the size and shape summary and the flowchart direction."""
    profile, problems = profile_of(block_text)
    if problems:
        return profile, problems, "", ""
    if profile == "sequence":
        found, participants, messages = check_sequence(block_text)
        return profile, found, f"{participants} participants and {messages} messages", ""
    if profile == "er":
        found, entities, relationships = check_er(block_text)
        return profile, found, f"{entities} entities and {relationships} relationships", ""
    if profile == "gantt":
        found, tasks, sections = check_gantt(block_text)
        return profile, found, f"{tasks} tasks in {sections} sections", ""
    if profile == "state":
        legacy = check_state_header(block_text)
        if legacy:
            return profile, legacy, "", ""
        diagram = mermaid_extract.parse_block(block)
        states = sum(1 for node in diagram.nodes if node.shape not in ("start", "end"))
        return profile, check_state(diagram, block_text), f"{states} states and {len(diagram.edges)} transitions", ""
    if profile == flowchart.ARCHITECTURE:
        text, backward = flowchart.rewrite_backward_edges(block_text)
        diagram = mermaid_extract.parse_block(mermaid_extract.SourceBlock(block.index, text, block.source_line))
        found = flowchart.check_architecture(diagram, block_text, backward)
    else:
        diagram = mermaid_extract.parse_block(block)
        found = flowchart.check_flow(diagram, block_text, profile)
    nodes = sum(1 for node in diagram.nodes if not node.container)
    measures, shape = layout.measure(diagram)
    return profile, found + measures, f"{nodes} nodes and {len(diagram.edges)} connectors, {shape}", diagram.direction


def check(path: Path) -> int:
    """Check every diagram in a model file, print the report and return the exit code."""
    try:
        blocks = mermaid_extract.load_blocks(path)
        results = [(block, check_block(block, block.text)) for block in blocks]
    except SystemExit:
        print(f"UNREADABLE {path}: the extractor refused it")
        return 2
    if not results:
        print(f"UNREADABLE {path}: no Mermaid block found")
        return 2
    failed, ways = 0, {}
    for number, (_, (profile, problems, size, direction)) in enumerate(results, 1):
        name = f"diagram {number}, {NAMES.get(profile, 'unknown')}"
        if problems:
            failed += 1
            for problem in problems:
                print(f"  {name}: {problem}")
        else:
            print(f"  {name}: ok, {size}")
        if profile in (flowchart.USER_FLOW, flowchart.PROCESS) and direction:
            ways.setdefault(profile, set()).add(flowchart.direction_family(direction))
    for profile, found in ways.items():
        if len(found) > 1:
            print(f"FAILED the {NAMES[profile]} diagrams in {path.name} run {' and '.join(sorted(found))}: "
                  "every diagram of one flow runs the same way")
            return 1
    if failed:
        print(f"FAILED {failed} of {len(results)} diagram(s) in {path.name}")
        return 1
    print(f"PASSED {len(results)} diagram(s) in {path.name}")
    return 0


# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 2. SELF-TEST
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# The shipped templates, the worked examples and their Project mirrors must
# keep passing the rules they teach. The mirrors are absent from a copy of the
# skill without the Project package, so a missing file is reported and not
# counted. A folder README under assets/ describes its files and the design
# file holds the board's style, so neither is a model.
KNOWLEDGE = PACKET.parent / "claude project" / "knowledge"
NOT_MODELS = {"README.md", "figjam-design.md"}
SHIPPED_MODELS = (
    sorted(p for p in (PACKET / "assets").rglob("*.md") if p.name not in NOT_MODELS)
    + [KNOWLEDGE / "Product Owner - Assets - Flow Templates.md"]
    + sorted(KNOWLEDGE.glob("Product Owner - Assets - Flow Templates - *.md"))
    + sorted(KNOWLEDGE.glob("Product Owner - Examples - Flow - *.md"))
)
STYLE_GUIDE = PACKET / "references" / "style-guide.md"
PALETTE_BLOCK = re.compile(r"<!-- FIGJAM_PALETTE:BEGIN -->(.*?)<!-- FIGJAM_PALETTE:END -->", re.S)
PALETTE_ROW = re.compile(
    r"^\|\s*([^|]+?)\s*\|\s*`(#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6})`\s*\|\s*`(#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6})`\s*"
    r"\|\s*([\d.]+):1\s*\|\s*([\d.]+):1\s*\|",
    re.M,
)


def palette_results() -> list[tuple[str, bool, str]]:
    """The style guide's palette record names exactly the pairs the check accepts, and its ratios measure true."""
    text = STYLE_GUIDE.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if STYLE_GUIDE.is_file() else ""
    block = PALETTE_BLOCK.search(text)
    if not block:
        return [("the style guide carries its palette record", False, f"no FIGJAM_PALETTE block in {STYLE_GUIDE}")]
    rows = PALETTE_ROW.findall(block.group(1))

# use_figma — Figma Plugin API Skill for FigJam

This skill contains FigJam-specific context for the `use_figma` MCP tool. The [figma-use](../figma-use/SKILL.md) skill provides foundational context for plugin API execution via MCP as well as the full Figma plugin API for more advanced use-cases that are not described here.

**Always include `figma-use-figjam` in the comma-separated `skillNames` parameter when calling `use_figma` for FigJam operations. If this skill was loaded via an MCP resource, you MUST prefix the name with `resource:` (e.g. `resource:figma-use-figjam`).** This is a logging parameter used to track skill usage — it does not affect execution.

> **FigJam URL is `figma.com/board/...`.** Do NOT call `figma.createPage()` in FigJam — it throws `TypeError: figma.createPage no such property 'createPage' on the figma global object`. `createPage()` is a Design-file API only (`figma.com/design/...`). FigJam files have a single implicit page; organize content with sections instead (see [create-section](references/create-section.md)).

## Inspecting FigJam Files

**`get_figjam` is the inspection tool for FigJam files.** It returns the full node tree as XML, including IDs of pages, sections, stickies, connectors, and other nodes you need to reference in subsequent `use_figma` calls.

- **Use `get_figjam` upfront** before writing any `use_figma` code that needs to reference existing nodes (page IDs, section IDs, etc.). Don't try to discover IDs by running an inspection script — `console.log` output from `use_figma` is **not returned to the agent** (see [figma-use Critical Rule #4](../figma-use/SKILL.md)). Only the `return` value comes back.
- **`get_metadata` does NOT work on FigJam files** — it is design-mode only and will fail immediately with "unsupported for FigJam files".
- **`get_screenshot` requires a valid `nodeId`** — passing an empty nodeId returns "invalid nodeId" error. Get IDs from `get_figjam` first.
- If you forgot to `return` an ID from a previous `use_figma` call and need it now, call `get_figjam` rather than re-running an inspection script.

## Loading Reference Docs Efficiently

Load only the references your task needs — but when you do need to load multiple, **issue all reads in a single parallel tool-call batch**, not sequentially across turns. For a typical board-creation task, that means a single message containing reads for `plan-board-content` plus the 3-4 specific node-type references you'll use.

## Deferred Tools — Batch-Load Schemas

The Figma MCP tools (`use_figma`, `get_figjam`, `get_screenshot`, `get_metadata`, `create_new_file`, `whoami`) often appear as deferred tools that require `ToolSearch` to load their schemas before they can be called. **Load all schemas in a single `ToolSearch` call** using the `select:` syntax instead of one call per tool:

```
ToolSearch query="select:use_figma,get_figjam,get_screenshot,get_metadata,create_new_file"
```

Six sequential `ToolSearch` calls is six round trips before any work happens. One batched call is one round trip.

## Text Mutations — Canonical Recipe

Every FigJam text mutation (sticky/shape/label/table cell/connector text, standalone text nodes) follows the same recipe as Design files: load font → `await` → mutate → return affected IDs. Skipping the load throws `Cannot write to node with unloaded font "<family> <style>"`. See [figma-use → gotchas.md → Canonical text-edit recipe](../figma-use/references/gotchas.md#canonical-text-edit-recipe-font-load--await--mutate--return-ids). FigJam-specific note: sublayer defaults vary (sticky → `Inter Medium`, shape → `Inter Medium`, connector → invalid until set), so always load from `node.text.fontName` rather than hardcoding `{ family: 'Inter', style: 'Regular' }`.

## Adding Images to a FigJam Board

**`upload_assets` is the ONLY supported way to add images to a FigJam file.** Call `upload_assets` with the FigJam `fileKey`; the tool returns single-use upload URLs that you POST raw image bytes to, and the image is committed and placed automatically. Pass `nodeIds` (with one entry per upload) to attach uploads to existing FigJam nodes as fills; omit `nodeIds` to drop the images onto the board as new layers.

For the full request/response shape, see [figma-use → api-reference.md → Images](../figma-use/references/api-reference.md#images).

## Reference Docs

- [plan-board-content](references/plan-board-content.md) - Read this for any board content request — board template, retro, brainstorm, ice breaker, meeting board, scaffold
  - Covers planning of generated board content, including sequential outline, sections, intents, and hierarchical text
  - Delegates to other references for specific API details
- [create-section](references/create-section.md) — Create and configure FigJam sections (sizing, naming, colors, content visibility, organizing nodes, column layouts)
- [create-sticky](references/create-sticky.md) — Create and configure FigJam sticky notes (colors, sizing, text, author visibility, batch creation)
- [create-connector](references/create-connector.md) — Create and configure FigJam connectors (endpoints, arrows, line types, labels, colors, diagram wiring)
- [create-text](references/create-text.md) — Create and configure FigJam text nodes (font loading, preset fonts and colors, sizing, lists, mind map operations)
- [position-figjam-nodes](references/position-figjam-nodes.md) — Position, size, and reparent nodes on the canvas (including within sections)
- [create-shape-with-text](references/create-shape-with-text.md) — Create and configure FigJam shapes with embedded text (shape types, color presets, sizing to fit text, diagram layouts)
- [create-code-block](references/create-code-block.md) — Create and configure FigJam code block nodes (languages, syntax highlighting, positioning, embedding in sections)
- [create-table](references/create-table.md) — Create and configure FigJam tables (rows, columns, cell text, color presets, resizing)

# Create Sticky Notes

> Part of the [figma-use-figjam skill](../SKILL.md). Creating, modifying, and styling sticky notes.

**Scope:** Sticky notes are FigJam-specific nodes created with `figma.createSticky()`. For advanced text formatting on stickies, see [edit-text](edit-text.md).

## When to use a Sticky

Use sticky notes for individual ideas, responses, or pieces of input — keep each sticky to one idea.

Do not use stickies for prompts, instructions, guiding questions, labels, or pre-written analysis — even if the content is short. If the content is there to guide or inform, use a text node instead.

For an interactive board, you can also think of a sticky as something an active participant or collaborator would have placed, whereas text is often a part of the board's structure.

## Creating a Sticky

```javascript
const sticky = figma.createSticky()

// Load the font before setting text content
await figma.loadFontAsync(sticky.text.fontName)
sticky.text.characters = 'Hello from FigJam!'

console.log('Created sticky:', sticky.id, sticky.text.characters)
figma.closePlugin()
```

## Setting Text

Stickies expose a `text` sublayer (a `TextSublayerNode`). You must load fonts before changing text content:

```javascript
const sticky = figma.createSticky()

// Load the font used by the sticky's text sublayer
await figma.loadFontAsync(sticky.text.fontName)
sticky.text.characters = 'Updated text'

figma.closePlugin()
```

To modify text on an existing sticky:

```javascript
const sticky = await figma.getNodeByIdAsync('123:456')
if (sticky && sticky.type === 'STICKY') {
  await figma.loadFontAsync(sticky.text.fontName)
  sticky.text.characters = 'New content'
}
figma.closePlugin()
```

## Color Palette

FigJam sticky notes use a fixed palette of 10 colors. Set via the `fills` property. For the canonical palette across all FigJam node types, see [figjam-colors](figjam-colors.md).

**CRITICAL**: Use `hex/255` notation (e.g. `0xA8/255`) for exact palette matching — rounded decimals cause FigJam to treat the color as "custom" instead of a palette color.

| Color  | Hex       |
| ------ | --------- |
| White  | `#FFFFFF` |
| Gray   | `#E6E6E6` |
| Green  | `#B3EFBD` |
| Teal   | `#B3F4EF` |
| Blue   | `#A8DAFF` |
| Violet | `#D3BDFF` |
| Pink   | `#FFA8DB` |
| Red    | `#FFB8A8` |
| Orange | `#FFD3A8` |
| Yellow | `#FFE299` |

### Setting a Sticky's Color

```javascript
const h = (r, g, b) => ({ r: r / 255, g: g / 255, b: b / 255 })

const sticky = figma.createSticky()
await figma.loadFontAsync(sticky.text.fontName)
sticky.text.characters = 'Blue sticky'
sticky.fills = [{ type: 'SOLID', color: h(0xa8, 0xda, 0xff) }] // Blue #A8DAFF

figma.closePlugin()
```

### Changing the Color of an Existing Sticky

```javascript
const h = (r, g, b) => ({ r: r / 255, g: g / 255, b: b / 255 })

const sticky = await figma.getNodeByIdAsync('123:456')
if (sticky && sticky.type === 'STICKY') {
  console.log('Before:', JSON.stringify(sticky.fills))
  sticky.fills = [{ type: 'SOLID', color: h(0xff, 0xe2, 0x99) }] // Yellow #FFE299
  console.log('After:', JSON.stringify(sticky.fills))
}
figma.closePlugin()
```

## Sizing

Stickies have two shapes controlled by `isWideWidth`:

- **Square** (default): `isWideWidth = false` — **240 × 240 px**
- **Wide rectangular**: `isWideWidth = true` — **416 × 240 px**

The `width` and `height` properties are **read-only**. Stickies do not support `resize()` — use `isWideWidth` to toggle between square and wide shapes.

**Auto-grow:** Stickies automatically grow taller when text overflows the default height. The width stays fixed (240 or 416), but height can exceed 240. When positioning multiple stickies, always read the actual `sticky.height` after setting text — don't assume 240.

Default to square stickies; only use wide stickies if the text is approximately 100 words or more.

```javascript
const sticky = figma.createSticky()
await figma.loadFontAsync(sticky.text.fontName)
sticky.text.characters = 'Wide sticky'
sticky.isWideWidth = true

console.log('Size:', sticky.width, 'x', sticky.height)
// Square: 240 x 240 (or taller if text overflows)
// Wide:   416 x 240 (or taller if text overflows)
figma.closePlugin()
```

### Toggling Size on an Existing Sticky

```javascript
const sticky = await figma.getNodeByIdAsync('123:456')
if (sticky && sticky.type === 'STICKY') {
  console.log('Before:', sticky.width, 'x', sticky.height, 'wide:', sticky.isWideWidth)
  sticky.isWideWidth = !sticky.isWideWidth
  console.log('After:', sticky.width, 'x', sticky.height, 'wide:', sticky.isWideWidth)
}
figma.closePlugin()
```

## Layout & Spacing (REQUIRED for batch creation)

**Use a grid, not a vertical stack.** When placing multiple stickies inside a section, arrange them in a **grid** (cols × rows) with 64 px spacing — do not stack them in a single column. See "Grid of Stickies" below.

**CRITICAL — Two-pass layout:** When creating multiple stickies, you MUST use a two-pass approach. Measuring one sticky and assuming all are the same size **will cause overlapping**.

**Pass 1 — Create all stickies:** Create every sticky, set its text and color. Do NOT position yet.

**Pass 2 — Position using actual dimensions:** Read each sticky's real `.width` and `.height`, compute per-row max heights, then assign x/y coordinates.

**Row-based positioning for grids:** When laying out stickies in a grid, position each row independently. Within a row, place stickies left-to-right using each sticky's actual `.width` plus uniform spacing. Rows should align vertically (use per-row max height for the y offset), but columns do NOT need to align across rows. This keeps uniform gaps between stickies even when widths vary (e.g., mixing square and wide stickies).

**Recommended spacing:** 20px minimum between stickies at all times. Use 30–40px for more breathing room. Default to 64px when laying out stickies in a grid pattern.

## Author Properties

Prefer to keep author visible unless explicitly prompted otherwise.

```javascript
const sticky = figma.createSticky()
await figma.loadFontAsync(sticky.text.fontName)
sticky.text.characters = 'Team feedback'

// The author is automatically set to the current user on creation
console.log('Author:', sticky.authorName)

// Hide or show the author label
sticky.authorVisible = false

figma.closePlugin()
```

## Batch Creation

### Row of Stickies

```javascript
const h = (r, g, b) => ({ r: r / 255, g: g / 255, b: b / 255 })
const labels = ['Idea 1', 'Idea 2', 'Idea 3', 'Idea 4']
const colors = [
  h(0xb3, 0xef, 0xbd), // Green #B3EFBD
  h(0xa8, 0xda, 0xff), // Blue #A8DAFF
  h(0xff, 0xa8, 0xdb), // Pink #FFA8DB
  h(0xff, 0xe2, 0x99), // Yellow #FFE299

const spacing = 64

// Pass 1: Create all stickies and set content.
// Every sticky uses the same default font, so load it once before the loop
// rather than awaiting per-iteration.
const probe = figma.createSticky()
await figma.loadFontAsync(probe.text.fontName)
probe.remove()
const stickies = []
for (let i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {
  const sticky = figma.createSticky()
  sticky.text.characters = labels[i]
  sticky.fills = [{ type: 'SOLID', color: colors[i % colors.length] }]
  stickies.push(sticky)
}

// Pass 2: Position using each sticky's actual width and height
const totalWidth = stickies.reduce((sum, s) => sum + s.width, 0) + (stickies.length - 1) * spacing
const maxH = Math.max(...stickies.map((s) => s.height))

# FigJam Node Positioning Tutorial

> Part of the [figma-use-figjam skill](../SKILL.md). Positioning, sizing, and reparenting nodes on the canvas.

Use this skill when working with positioning, sizing, and reparenting nodes.

## Basics of how nodes are positioned

Nodes may be positioned by setting their `x` and `y` properties. Nodes are positioned with respect to their parent.

```javascript
// Position (relative to parent)
node.x = 100
node.y = 200
```

## Positioning Nodes Relative to Existing Nodes

It's important to remember that `node.x` and `node.y` are relative to the node's parent, not the page. For example: a node inside a section has coordinates relative to that section's origin.

When creating or placing a node relative to an existing node:

1. **Find the parent**: Locate the parent of the existing node.
2. **Add new node to parent**: Call `parent.appendChild()` to add the new node to the parent.
3. **Position within parent**: Position the new node within the parent. The x / y coordinates of the new node will be with respect to the top-left corner of the parent.
4. **Ensure parent sections encompass their children**: If the parent is a section:
   a. Resize the section to encompass the new node
   b. (see [create-section](create-section.md) — "Resizing an Existing Section" for more info)

Example helper function:

```javascript
// existingNodeId (string): the node id you are positioning relative to
// nodeToPosition: the node you are trying to position relative to the existing node
async function placeNodeRelativeToOtherNode(existingNodeId, nodeToPosition) {

  // 1: find the parent of existing node
  const existingNode = await figma.getNodeByIdAsync(existingNodeId);
  const parent = existingNode.parent

  // 2: add the node to the parent
  parent.appendChild(nodeToPosition)

  // 3: position the node w.r.t the top-left corner of the parent
  // here, we chose to place it to the right of the existing node
  nodeToPosition.x = existingNode.x + existingNode.width + 40;
  nodeToPosition.y = existingNode.y;

  // 4: if the parent is a section: resize the section if needed
  if (parent.type === 'SECTION') {
    // ... resize if needed, (see [create-section](create-section.md) — "Resizing an Existing Section" for more info)
  }
}
```

## Adding Nodes to a Section

Use `appendChild` to move existing nodes into a section.

**CRITICAL**: when you call `appendChild`, the node's x/y coordinates become relative to the **section's local coordinate space**, where (0,0) is the top-left corner of the section — NOT absolute board coordinates. Always call `appendChild` **first**, then set the node's position using section-local coordinates.

**IMPORTANT:** After adding nodes to a section, you MUST check that the section encompasses its children. Refer to the `Resizing an Existing Section` code snippet for reference. This is _crucial_ for a high-quality output.

Steps:

1. **Add new node to parent**: Call `parent.appendChild()` to add the new node to the parent.
2. **Position within parent**: Position the new node within the parent. The x / y coordinates of the new node will be with respect to the TL of the parent.
3. **Clean up any layout consequences**: If the parent is a section:
   a. Resize the section to encompass the new node
   b. (see [create-section](create-section.md) — "Resizing an Existing Section" for more info)

Example helper function:

```javascript
function addNodeToSection(node, section) {
  // Ensure this is a section
  if (section.type !== 'SECTION') {
    console.log('The node provided is not a section')
    return
  }

  // Append FIRST, then position using section-local coordinates
  section.appendChild(node)
  node.x = 32
  node.y = 32
  console.log(`Moved ${node.name} into ${section.name}`)

  // ... resize section if needed, (see [create-section](create-section.md) — "Resizing an Existing Section" for more info)
}
```

### Setting a Section's Color

```javascript
const h = (r, g, b) => ({ r: r / 255, g: g / 255, b: b / 255 })

const section = figma.createSection()
section.name = 'Blue section'
section.resize(400, 300)
section.fills = [{ type: 'SOLID', color: h(0xf5, 0xfb, 0xff) }] // Light blue #F5FBFF

figma.closePlugin()
```

### Changing the Color of an Existing Section

```javascript
const h = (r, g, b) => ({ r: r / 255, g: g / 255, b: b / 255 })

const section = await figma.getNodeByIdAsync('123:456')
if (section && section.type === 'SECTION') {
  console.log('Before:', JSON.stringify(section.fills))
  section.fills = [{ type: 'SOLID', color: h(0xeb, 0xff, 0xee) }] // Light green #EBFFEE
  console.log('After:', JSON.stringify(section.fills))
}
figma.closePlugin()
```

## Hiding Section Contents

Toggle whether a section's child nodes are visible:

```javascript
const section = await figma.getNodeByIdAsync('123:456')
if (section && section.type === 'SECTION') {
  console.log('Contents hidden before:', section.sectionContentsHidden)
  section.sectionContentsHidden = true
  console.log('Contents hidden after:', section.sectionContentsHidden)
}
figma.closePlugin()
```

## Adding Nodes to a Section

**CRITICAL**: It's very important that you follow the instructions in [position-figjam-nodes](position-figjam-nodes.md): Adding Nodes to a Section. This is _crucial_ for a high-quality output.

## Cloning Sections

```javascript
const original = await figma.getNodeByIdAsync('123:456')
if (original && original.type === 'SECTION') {
  const clone = original.clone()
  clone.x = original.x + original.width + 32
  clone.name = original.name + ' (copy)'
  console.log('Cloned section:', clone.id, clone.name)
}
figma.closePlugin()
```

## Key Points

- **Always wrap code in an async IIFE:** `(async () => { ... })();`
- **Always call `figma.closePlugin()`** at the end of every code path.
- **Use `section.resize(width, height)`** to set section size — `width`/`height` are read-only. Sections also accept `resizeWithoutConstraints(...)`, but `resize(...)` is the preferred method.
- **Resize sections to fit their children.** After adding children to a section, make sure that the section encompasses the children. If you need to resize it, refer to the example of resizing an existing section.
- **Use node IDs** from the user message, not `figma.currentPage.selection`.

Then check the overview for stretching, a label cut off, overlap, a connector crossing, an edge that reads as joining the wrong node, a colour that does not match its entry in the key and whether the board answers the `userIntent` sentence. A finding there goes on a `Finding:` line of the reply, and it is fixed only by reshaping the model and recomposing after a yes, inside the two-attempt bound Section 9 sets. Section 7 names the read for each route. The rows that fail silently are read back the same way, one at a time and before the gate. Each provenance row whose class is not current behavior or whose edge is inferred gets one re-read of its source, and that row records the reason. A row that quotes a source line is not re-read
69:11. **Reply.** Deliver as Section 8 sets out

234:- A contradicted item is never removed in silence. It goes to the reply's `Left out:` line with both sources and the reason, or the gate's one question asks which source governs and that answer settles it. Nothing is dropped without a trace and no new line is added for it
315:- **Named omissions.** Every cut, every split and every point the sources left open appears in the reply's `Left out:` line, never dropped silently
353:- Read the written board back with `get_figjam`, as Section 7 sets out. When the server reports no read tool, the read-back is not possible and the reply says so. When the connected tools include no read tool, the line is `Read-back: not possible, the connector has no read tool`, and the board is never called done. When the board URL landed in a re-saved artifact, the line ends with the name of the file the artifact was saved to. On a matched read-back the same line also names the first glance in one clause, such as `, first glance: the failed payment`, so the user knows what should win before the board is opened
426:- When the write added extensions, the next line counts them: `Extensions: 4 of 4 pins, 4 of 4 legend stickies, 0 overlaps`, or `Extensions: 2 of 2 notes, 0 overlaps` for single stickies
427:- When the provenance table lists items left out, the next line names them as `Left out: <item>, <reason>`, so the user sees what the board does not hold. On a split or a cut, the reason names the detail level and the cut, such as `Left out: the retry path, split into a second diagram`
430:- A finding from the read-back, a warning the write returned, a `DESIGN` line the composer printed, an open item or a question the user must answer is one `Finding:` line each, placed above the self-scan. A `DESIGN` finding names the token, what the design file asked for and the value the board drew instead. Where the board landed, the tools used, the cleanup and the rollback are not part of the reply
431:- The last line is the HVR self-scan in the shape `AGENTS.md` step 8 sets, counted on the labels written to the board. Nothing follows it, not a note, a finding or a question. Flow Mode is exempt from the export steps, never from the scan
The check enforces these on every diagram, and each type adds its own in `references/types/`.

- **No emoji, no markup and no literal `\n`.** The board shows every label exactly as the model writes it, so markup would land as literal characters, and the `generate_diagram` fallback rejects emoji and a literal `\n`. Markup means an HTML tag, emphasis stars or underscores and backticks, anywhere in the block but a `%%` comment
- **Labels of at most 40 characters on one line.** Detail moves onto an edge label or into a second node
- **camelCase ids.** Letters and digits only, starting with a letter. No underscore, which breaks connector routing on the `generate_diagram` fallback, and never `end`, `subgraph`, `graph` or another Mermaid keyword. The composer names every layer after its id, such as `node:refund` and `edge:refund->done`, so the read-back finds each one by name
- **A budget per type.** sk-design-diagram's general budget of 9 nodes and 12 connectors applies unless the type sets its own. Over budget, split rather than shrink, and offer the overview board and the detail board together rather than choosing one quietly
- **Allocate before the first block.** The ordered source list is divided into diagram-sized groups before any Mermaid is written, each group ending on a hand-off node and named after that hand-off, so the ledger checks an allocation rather than a model that already overran. A group still over budget takes the fixed cut order the hand-judged rules below give
- **Colour by meaning.** The composer colours every node by its kind in the design `assets/figjam-design.md` holds, as `references/style-guide.md` Section 2 sets out, so the same colour means the same thing on every board and the model never colours a node for looks. A user flow and a process each carry exactly one `style` line, which marks the first glance. A styled goal, failing end or decision keeps its kind and takes a pink outline, and a styled step is drawn light pink. The other types take no `style` line and may name the first glance with a `%% focus:` comment line, which is refused where it names nothing, as `references/style-guide.md` Section 3 sets out. The pairs come from the style guide, and the check refuses a second accent. Colour marks a kind and never a team, and the rule holds for the reply text and the key as well as the fills, so no sentence or key entry ties a colour or a zone tint to a team
- **The composer owns the layout.** Never move a composed node or rewire its connectors. A layout that reads badly is fixed by splitting the diagram or reshaping the model and composing it again, not by dragging. The levers that reshape a layout are named at the end of this section. The composer tags the board it draws, and a tag changes nothing a reader sees, as Section 6 sets out

Judged by hand, on every type:

- **Restraint.** Every node is a distinct idea, every connector carries information and no label repeats its shape
- **The source's words.** Labels use the product's or the source's own terms
- **Splits cut in order.** Decoration first, then exact duplicates, then items that change nothing a reader decides, then cross-cutting items such as logging. Still over, split into an overview and a detail
- **Named omissions.** Every cut, every split and every point the sources left open appears in the reply's `Left out:` line, never dropped silently

### What a redraw changes

A cramped or tangled board is fixed in the Mermaid, because no composed node is ever moved. The composer ranks the steps by the longest path from the start, keeps the longest route that stays on the path on one straight line, the spine, and sets every branch beside it. Five things in the block reach that layout, and no sixth thing does:

| Lever | What it changes | Where it stops |
|---|---|---|
| The direction | `LR` runs the flow across the board and `TD` stacks it down, so one direction reads tight where the other reads open. Write `LR` for a user flow or a process unless the chain is short, because a board reads wider than it reads tall | A long chain stays long either way, and a sequence and a gantt fix their own direction |
| The zones | A `%% zone:` line groups steps in a tinted section, in flow order on a user flow or a process without lanes and around the entities on an ER diagram. Lanes and composite states are zones already | Once a flow has zones every node sits in one, a node sits in one zone at most, and the check refuses a zone that names no node |
| The order the nodes are declared | The composer keeps declaration order wherever the edges leave a tie, so the step written first sits first in its rank | A stated edge still wins, because the layout follows the connections |
| The edge set | One edge fewer removes a line that crosses the board, and one edge more pulls two parts together. The edges also decide the spine | Every edge kept carries information, so a cut changes what the board says |
| The goal | A `style` line on an end makes it the goal, and the spine runs to it. With none marked, the end the longest path reaches is the goal | One accent, so one end is the goal |

Three commands look like levers and are not:
- `a & b --> c` groups nothing, and only a zone or a subgraph groups, so write one edge per line
- `a ~~~ b` is an invisible link, which places nothing where the model asks, and the check refuses it
- `a ---> b` is a length hint that neither the composer nor the generated fallback honours. The extra dashes draw the same line, and the check refuses them

---

## 6. WRITE ROUTES

### Composed route, primary

Flow Mode composes the board itself. `scripts/compose_board.py` reads the checked model and fills `assets/compose-board.js`, and one `use_figma` call runs that code in the file the gate named. The call draws a framed board: the title and the subtitle, the diagram with its zones, every shape sized to its text and coloured by its kind, the routed connectors, a key of every mark the board uses and the source line, all on an 8 pixel grid. It draws every type in Section 3.

The route is a native MCP connection to Figma's server at `https://mcp.figma.com/mcp`, which Figma's own plugin declares in its root `mcp.json`. The connection comes from that plugin or from the client's connector. Code Mode holds no manual for Figma's hosted server here, and its `figma` manual runs Framelink's `figma-developer-mcp` instead. Whether Figma's OAuth-gated server would admit a Code Mode client is unverified. The vendored `mcp-figma` packet's wiring guide covers that Code Mode path, and its Section 6 records how a headless Claude Code or Codex child reaches the hosted server. The `allowed-tools` frontmatter of this packet names Code Mode as its only MCP tool and no native tool, because the native names depend on the client. Claude Code serves them under the name its config gives the server, such as `mcp__figma-remote__use_figma`. Codex serves them through the Figma app on the ChatGPT account as `figma.use_figma`, and `codex exec` refuses that call with "MCP tool call requires approval" until the client's config approves app tools. That refusal is a client setting and not a Figma outage.

- List the connected tools first and use the names and input fields the server reports. Once a board's `fileKey` is known, on a new board, a revision or a read of a board written earlier, call `create_session` with it and pass the returned session id on every later call for this work. The route needs `use_figma` and `get_figjam`, and a new board also needs `whoami` and `create_new_file`. Load Figma's `figma-use` and `figma-use-figjam` skills before the first `use_figma` call, as Figma requires, and pass their names in `skillNames`. Flow Mode's rules win where the two differ
- Name the plan before the gate, because an account can hold plans that belong to other organizations. Call `whoami` and read the plans it returns. `whoami` says which plans the account holds and not which plan owns a board, so a plan it returns settles a new file only. On a new file one plan is named in the gate, and several plans become one question about which team the board belongs to, asked before the gate. A revision writes into a board whose plan was set when it was made, so on a revision the gate names the board and states its plan only when the user supplied it
- A new board starts with `create_new_file`, after the yes, with `editorType` set to `figjam`, `planKey` set to the plan the gate named and `fileName` set to the board's title. Load Figma's own skill for that tool first where the server offers one. Every later diagram of the same work and every revision passes that file's `fileKey`, so the work stays on one board
- Compose each diagram with `python3 scripts/compose_board.py <model file> --diagram <n> --out <code file>`, run on the model file the check passed and writing outside the repository. Exit 0 prints a `COMPOSED` line with the counts the read-back will look for and the name of the design the board is drawn in. Each design warning prints a `DESIGN` line before it and the `COMPOSED` line counts them: a token that cannot stand draws its shipped value, and a design file that cannot be read draws the shipped design whole. Exit 1 means the model fails the check, or the code runs past the 50,000 characters one call takes, and the failure line then says how many of them a team design's `THEME` takes. Either is fixed by splitting the diagram, never by trimming the code. Paste the code file's text unchanged as the `use_figma` code, one diagram per call
- The call returns the board id, the tag, the counts drawn beside the counts the model expects, every node and connector it drew with its id, any warnings and a screenshot of the whole board. A warning is a finding, reported as measured like a read-back mismatch
- A new board lands 400 pixels to the right of everything already on the page, its top level with the highest node there, so it never covers existing content and the diagrams of one piece of work read left to right in the order they were written
- The composer tags the board section it draws with shared plugin data under the fixed namespace `productowner`, keyed by the board's title, with the write time and the counts as the value. The title is the key because a later session can rebuild it, and it cannot rebuild an earlier run id. The tag carries nothing from the source material beyond the title the board already shows, because any plugin that can open the board can read shared plugin data. A refused tag becomes a warning and the board stands
- The tag departs from Figma's rule to keep workflow state outside the Figma file, because Flow Mode writes no file of its own, so the board is the only place a later session can learn what an earlier one wrote
- A failed or timed-out call is not proof that nothing landed. When `use_figma` reports `safeToRetryWithoutCanvasRead: true`, fix the error and retry once. Otherwise read the file with `get_figjam` before a retry, and retry only when the board is absent
- Read the written board back with `get_figjam`, as Section 7 sets out. When the server reports no read tool, the read-back is not possible and the reply says so. A read refused because the Starter plan or the View or Collab seat has spent its six tool calls for the month gives `Read-back: not possible` with that limit named, and the board is never called done
- Never move or restyle a composed node afterwards. Additions follow `references/hybrid-workflow.md`
- The rollback for a new file is that file. The rollback for an existing board is to delete the one board section the write returned, which removes everything drawn inside it, through `use_figma` and only on a reply that names it or a yes to a question that names it, as the delete rule below sets out. A later session finds the boards an earlier one wrote by reading the tag on every section at the top of the page, `figma.currentPage.children.filter((n) => n.type === 'SECTION' && n.getSharedPluginDataKeys('productowner').length)`. Stop if the section to delete carries no returned id and no tag. With no read tool nothing is deleted, and the user removes the board by hand
- A revision request opens with a playback of the rows it changes, which waits for its answer before the gate. It composes the new board first, reads it back and then asks whether to delete the old board section found by its tag. The delete waits for its own yes to a question that names the old board by its title, so the yes that covered the compose never covers the delete, and with no second yes both boards stay. Composing first means a failed write never leaves the user with no board at all, and the tag means a revision in a new session replaces a board rather than drawing a second one beside it
- A delete of anything that was on the file before this write runs only on a reply that names the boards it removes, or on a yes to a question that names exactly those boards by title. A bare "yes" or "go ahead", the gate's yes and an answer to a question that named no board never delete such a board. The question lists every board the delete removes, and the delete removes those and no other. A board this conversation did not write, whether an earlier session or another person wrote it, is deleted only when the user's request is about that board, such as a revision of it, and never to tidy the page. Rolling back what this write added is not such a delete: it follows the rollback rule above, or the extension rollback in `references/hybrid-workflow.md`, each on its own yes to the deletion
- A board that holds two or more diagrams is planned before the first write, as `references/hybrid-workflow.md` Section 8 sets out

### Generated route, fallback

When `use_figma` is not among the connected tools and `generate_diagram` is, Figma's generator draws the diagram from the Mermaid block instead. Its board is plainer: the generator sets its own font, colours and layout, draws no title, zone or key and strips every `%%` line, so the title, subtitle, source and zone lines do not reach it. Figma marks `generate_diagram` as remote only, so a session connected only to Figma's desktop server has no `generate_diagram` and falls to the `fj` route or to No route. Load Figma's own diagram skill first where the runtime offers it.

- Send one diagram per call, with `name` set to a distinct title that matches its hand-off, `mermaidSyntax` set to the block and `userIntent` set to the reader's question in one sentence. An architecture also passes `useArchitectureLayoutCode` as `"FIGMA_DIAGRAM_2026"`, and no other type passes it
- The first call carries no `fileKey`, so the tool creates a new file. Every later diagram of the same work and every revision passes that file's `fileKey`. Never call a separate create-file tool first on this route
- Read the diagram back with `get_figjam` by label, as Section 7 sets out for a board with no layer names. A failed or timed-out call is read before a retry, and when the first call failed there is no `fileKey` to read, so ask the user to look for a new file in their FigJam drafts before a retry
- This route adds nothing beside the diagram, because a title, a tag, a note and a deletion all need `use_figma`. The gate says so, and the reply names the missing tool. The rollback for a new file is that file, and on an existing board the user removes the diagram by hand

### `fj` route, fallback

`figma-ds-cli` writes node by node into the FigJam file open in Figma Desktop. It needs version 1.2.0 or later from the silships repository, because the npm build has no `fj` group, and its local daemon running. The vendored `mcp-figma/SKILL.md` owns the connection, the daemon and the mutating gate.

- The route draws a user flow, and a process with no lanes that uses only the user-flow shapes. Every other type needs a hosted route, because `fj` has no layout, container or table verb. It draws the diagram alone, with no title, zone or key
- On this route the target file is the FigJam file open in Figma Desktop. Confirm with the read-only `fj info` that it is a FigJam board before the first write, and name it in the gate. Every FigJam verb fails on a design file
- `fj shape` per node: `--type ELLIPSE` for a start or end, `RECTANGLE` for a step, `DIAMOND` for a decision and a small `ELLIPSE` for a merge dot. Every position is computed, because `fj` has no layout verb
- `fj connect` per edge. It takes no label, so each edge label is its own `fj text` node beside the connector
- Read node ids back with `fj nodes -l` between steps when a create verb prints none, and read the finished diagram the same way. Each edge label is an `fj text` node, which the read-back counts as a label, never as a node
- `fj delete` and `fj eval` stay off this path. Each needs an explicit request and the destructive ceremony in `mcp-figma/`
- The rollback is Undo in the session, or a restore from the file's version history. A FigJam file has one page, so there is no page to duplicate first

### No route

When no route is reachable, or the type needs a hosted route and neither `use_figma` nor `generate_diagram` is connected, say which one is missing and what it needs. Offer the checked model in the reply for the user to keep. Never render the diagram as an image, an HTML page or a Mermaid file as a stand-in for the board.

When the type is one the `fj` route draws, a user flow or a process with no lanes, and `figma-ds-cli` is missing or not connected, the reply also names its setup. The vendored `../mcp-figma/` packet owns these steps and their scripts:

1. Install it once with `bash mcp-figma/scripts/install.sh` from the repository root, then confirm `figma-ds-cli --version` prints 1.2.0 or later
2. Import the bridge once: in Figma Desktop, choose Plugins, then Development, then Import plugin from manifest, and pick `~/.figma-ds-cli/source/plugin/manifest.json`, where the install puts it. The folder is hidden, so on macOS press Cmd+Shift+G in the file picker and paste the path
3. In each session, open the target FigJam file, run Plugins, then Development, then FigCli, keep it open, and connect with `figma-ds-cli connect --safe`

On the composed route the read is `get_figjam` on the board id the write returned. It reports each section by name, each shape with its label text and each connector with its layer name and its two endpoint ids, so the board is matched to the model by name and by id:

- A node is a shape whose id the write returned in its node list, carrying the label the model gives it. Shapes inside the `Key` section are samples, and the empty 16 pixel ellipses are anchors that hold a routed connector, so neither counts as a node
- A connector is a connector named `edge:<from>-><to>`, one per model edge. A routed edge reaches its target through anchors, so its start is an anchor rather than the source: follow the connectors named `leg:<from>-><to>:<n>`, from the highest `<n>` down to `:1`, back through their anchors to the source node. The label sits on the leg that carries it
- A sequence message is named `edge:<from>-><to>:<n>`, with its order as the last part. Its ends hold anchors on the two lifelines rather than the participant boxes, so the name carries both parties and the screenshot shows the line between them
- A zone is a section named after its label, and its nodes sit inside it

On the generated route the read is `get_figjam`, node by node, matching shapes by their label because the generator writes no layer names. On the `fj` route it is `fj nodes -l`. When only a screenshot could be read, the read was visual, because a picture cannot prove which nodes a connector joins.

A board that already holds content can be slower to read than a fresh one. A read that times out is retried on fewer nodes at a time, halving the count until the read returns. A timeout is never proof that a node or a connector is missing. When the file held content before the write, the read-back reads those nodes again and compares their count, position and size with the read taken before the write, so the reply can say the content already there was left as it was.

---

## 8. DELIVERY

The reply carries the board, its proof and the self-scan, and nothing else. Anything the user must know or answer has a place above the self-scan.

- The first line is the board URL
- The second line is the read-back, counts measured on the board against the model, in the words the type's reference uses: `Read-back: 8 of 8 nodes, 8 of 8 connectors, 2 of 2 decision exits labelled`. When the connected tools include no read tool, the line is `Read-back: not possible, the connector has no read tool`, and the board is never called done. When the board URL landed in a re-saved artifact, the line ends with the name of the file the artifact was saved to. On a matched read-back the same line also names the first glance in one clause, such as `, first glance: the failed payment`, so the user knows what should win before the board is opened
- When the write added extensions, the next line counts them: `Extensions: 4 of 4 pins, 4 of 4 legend stickies, 0 overlaps`, or `Extensions: 2 of 2 notes, 0 overlaps` for single stickies
- When the provenance table lists items left out, the next line names them as `Left out: <item>, <reason>`, so the user sees what the board does not hold. On a split or a cut, the reason names the detail level and the cut, such as `Left out: the retry path, split into a second diagram`
- A contradicted item appears in that same line with both of its sources and the reason it was not drawn, so a finding the sources disagree on is still visible to the reader
- When the file holds two or more diagrams, the read-back line also names the board a reader opens first, by the ordinal and the name in its title, in one clause such as `, start here: 1. Signup`
- A finding from the read-back, a warning the write returned, a `DESIGN` line the composer printed, an open item or a question the user must answer is one `Finding:` line each, placed above the self-scan. A `DESIGN` finding names the token, what the design file asked for and the value the board drew instead. Where the board landed, the tools used, the cleanup and the rollback are not part of the reply
- The last line is the HVR self-scan in the shape `AGENTS.md` step 8 sets, counted on the labels written to the board. Nothing follows it, not a note, a finding or a question. Flow Mode is exempt from the export steps, never from the scan
- A read-back that does not match is reported as measured, with the missing or extra items named. The board is never called done on a mismatch
- A paired request, a route carrying `then: "FLOW"`, delivers the artifact first under its own mode's protocol: written, exported and read back. That reply ends on Flow Mode's playback, which waits for its own answer, with no ClickUp offer. Flow Mode then runs with that artifact as its product-doc source, under its own pre-write check and its own yes at the write gate
- When the request came with an artifact and the read-back matched the model, a Task, Bug, Story or Epic uses its `Flows` group and a Doc uses `Related references`, with the diagram’s name as the link text. The paired-output route and link placement are owned here
- The artifact is then saved again at its existing export path and read back, so the file the user keeps carries the link. That save is the artifact's own export step, not a Flow Mode one
- When only a screenshot could be read, the read-back line ends with `, read visually`
- No file is written to `export/`, and no Mermaid, HTML, SVG or PNG file is left behind. The check reads the model from a temporary file outside the repository, deleted once the reply is sent

### The playback

Each round of intake opens with a short replay of the rows settled so far, one row per line, each in the words the product uses. The replay sits above the round's next question, so a wrong row is corrected before more answers build on it.

Before the model there is one full playback, and it waits for one answer. It states the Brief's question and its outcome, what each source settled, every row still open and every fact it assumed. That answer is not the gate's yes, because the gate asks about a write and the playback asks about the reading.

An unanswered question never stops the work. The reading proceeds on the recommendation the question gave, the fact is marked assumed and the playback names it, so the user corrects it before anything is written. A yes moves the work on to the model. A correction changes that row and the playback runs again over the rows it touched.

The playback is not one of the five reply lines. It runs before the write, and the reply states only the board, the read-back, the extensions, what was left out and the self-scan.

### The gate is its own reply

The playback and the gate are two replies, never one. The playback comes before the model, so its reply carries no Mermaid, no check result and no composed code. It ends on its one question about the reading, names no plan, lists no calls and never asks whether to write. The gate reply follows the playback's answer, and its one question asks about the write alone. No question is ever worded so that one yes covers both, such as a yes that confirms the reading and the write together.

Only a yes to the gate's own question writes. A yes to the playback, an answer to an intake round, a request to use the recommended answers or a yes to a question no reply asked never writes. Before the playback has had its answer, the reply to any of those is the playback. Once it has, and the gate has not been shown yet, the reply is the gate, and the write waits for the yes that answers it. A request to use the recommended answers sent after the playback counts as the playback's answer.

---

## 9. ERROR RECOVERY

### The check fails

Fix the named rule, or split the diagram at a natural hand-off, and run the check again. Never write a model the check failed.
